old: It began as a shouted command urging soldiers to grab what they'd fight with.
Its Old Italian ancestor literally meant 'to the weapons!'
It's a distant cousin of the everyday word 'arms,' both from Latin arma.
clues: This noun for a kind of signal began life as a real shout on the battlefield, a cry ordering soldiers to grab their weapons.
Today it means any sound or signal that warns of danger, like a ringing fire bell, more urgent than a simple warning and broader than just a siren.
You set one on your bedside clock to wake up, and a false one sends everyone outside for nothing. It shares its root with the word 'arms.'
